budget_constraint.detail: WebSearch returned 'session has used its web search budget (200 of 200)' on my first four calls, before any research began (apparently consumed by the six threads dispatched before this one). All discovery in this thread was performed via WebFetch — either against officially-guessed/known URLs, or via DuckDuckGo's HTML endpoint (html.duckduckgo.com) used as a search substitute through WebFetch. Flagged to team-lead in real time; team-lead confirmed the budget itself would not be raised and directed me to pivot toward WebFetch-native, constructible-URL territory (privacy/security, manufacturer documentation) and to defer rather than fabricate anything requiring genuine discovery.
what_this_cost: Reddit community-consensus sourcing (explicitly prioritized as a tier-3 source type in the brief) was effectively unavailable: reddit.com, old.reddit.com, and the Reddit JSON endpoint all failed to fetch in this environment ('unable to fetch'). DuckDuckGo surfaced thread titles only (e.g. 'Tips on how to keep your LDR ~spicy~'), never actual comment content, so zero Reddit claims made it into this report.

App Store privacy-label verification for Kiiroo, Lovense, and We-Vibe's apps failed: without search, I could not reliably locate the correct official app listing. Two candidate URLs surfaced via DuckDuckGo — a 'WeVibe' app made by 'The Happy Broadcast' (a relationship-conversation-starter app, unrelated to Standard Innovation's We-Vibe hardware) and a 'FeelConnect 3' app by 'Feel Robotics B.V.' whose listing made no reference to Kiiroo — were both checked directly and discarded as unconfirmed rather than used. This is a discovery failure, not a verification failure: I could check candidates but not reliably find the right ones.

Lovense's shipping-to-Israel and sync mechanics (real-time vs. async, cellular vs. wifi-only) remain UNKNOWN after five separate attempts across official Lovense pages (lovense.com/long-distance-sex-toys, /faq, /shipping-info, /shipping-policy, /faq/Shipping/) and DuckDuckGo search substitutes.

The anticipation/build-up framing (a must_cover item, explicitly named in the brief as the thread's most novel territory) could not be discovery-sourced to real, documented couples' practices. The three entries built around it (t7-overnight-fell-asleep-to-woke-up-to, t7-lunch-break-discreet-anticipation, t7-friday-sunday-slow-build) are grounded in a real, verified peer-reviewed source (Van Dijck et al. 2025) for WHY delayed/asynchronous intimate messaging works, but the specific delivery mechanics are this report's own structured design built on top of that finding, not a discovered ritual from an identifiable couple. This is disclosed inline in each entry's own timezone_friction field and repeated here for visibility, per team-lead's instruction that a guessed source is worse than an honest hole.
must_cover_items_underserved: ANTICIPATION AND BUILD-UP ACROSS THE 7-HOUR GAP — served with research-grounded but self-designed practices, not discovered real-couple rituals. A round-2 pass with search restored should specifically hunt reddit.com/r/LongDistance, r/LDR, and similar for documented anticipation rituals to either confirm, replace, or add alongside these three entries.

Device data-collection/retention practices for Kiiroo and Lovense specifically — only We-Vibe's documented 2016-17 history and current policy-link presence were confirmed via primary/tertiary sources; the other two named manufacturers in the brief remain unverified on this specific point.

App-permission and Bluetooth/cloud-relay model of connected devices (explicitly named in the brief's privacy must_cover) — not delivered for any of the three named device categories; this requires either working search or hand-supplied correct App Store URLs for a round 2 to verify.

activities.name: Sleep with something that smells like them
activities.one_liner: Each partner keeps a shirt or pillowcase the other has worn near the bed at night, using scent as a physiological substitute for physical presence at bedtime.
how_it_works: One partner wears a plain cotton t-shirt (or sleeps on a pillowcase) for a day/night without deodorant, cologne, or scented laundry products.
It's exchanged during an in-person visit, or the couple's initial exchange is simply kept and re-worn/refreshed on a rotating basis rather than repeatedly re-mailed.
The other partner keeps it on or near their pillow and sleeps with it during their sleepy, wind-down window.
No app and no call needed — this runs in the background of the relationship, independent of the call schedule.
tools_needed: a worn cotton garment or pillowcase
activities.timezone_friction: Purely passive — no live coordination needed, so it tolerates the 7h gap trivially. Tagged only w1 because this is specifically a bedtime ritual; it has no relevance to daytime windows.

activities.name: Totwoo synced touch jewelry
activities.one_liner: Paired smart jewelry that lights up and vibrates on the partner's matching piece the instant you tap your own — a silent, screen-free 'thinking of you' that works at any distance.
how_it_works: Both partners buy and pair a matched set (e.g. Soulmate 2.0 or a Milan Rope bracelet) via the Totwoo app — this one-time setup is the only screen time the activity needs.
Tap or press your piece any time during the day; the paired device on the other person's wrist/hand lights up and vibrates in real time, wherever they are.
Custom light/vibration patterns can be assigned agreed meanings (e.g. 'thinking of you' vs. 'call me when free').
The app also supports scheduled 'love letters' timed to arrive later, and call alerts.
activities.cost: paid ($139-$179 per matched pair for the bestselling styles)
activities.timezone_friction: A silent tap needs no shared window at all, which is why it spans w1 (bedside, silent), w3 (worn on the wrist, no screen needed while walking/commuting), w4 (a discreet tap at a desk reads as nothing to a coworker), and w8/w9 (works all day regardless of who's free). Confirmed to ship to Israel with an explicit regional pricing tier (Fast Express ~$9.9 under $150, free over $150, VIP $39.9/5-7 days) — this is the device in this thread that clears the Israel-shipping bar that Bond Touch (not listed) and Kiiroo (not listed) do not.

activities.name: Send a heartbeat or tap over Messages (Digital Touch)
activities.one_liner: Use the built-in Digital Touch feature in Messages/Apple Watch to send a live heartbeat, a tap, or a sketch that appears and vibrates on their device — free, since you already both have Apple devices.
how_it_works: Open a conversation in Messages, or use Digital Touch on Apple Watch, with your partner.
Tap and hold with two fingers to send your live heartbeat, tap once to send a single tap, or sketch with one finger.
It's delivered like any other message — it doesn't require both people to be on a call, awake, or nearby.
The recipient sees or feels it whenever they next check their phone or watch.
tools_needed: Apple Watch (optional, for the heartbeat sensor)
activities.timezone_friction: Delivered asynchronously exactly like a text, so it tolerates the full 7h gap and any window — tagged w1/w3/w4/w8/w9 because those are exactly the moments a 2-second silent gesture fits. Could not confirm from Apple's own documentation whether delivery ever depends on local Bluetooth proximity vs. iMessage/internet delivery; three independent tech-press write-ups describe it purely as a Messages feature sent 'to a contact,' consistent with internet delivery, but that is corroboration, not a primary-source confirmation.

activities.name: App-controlled toy, live session (Kiiroo FeelConnect)
activities.one_liner: App-controlled interactive toys (Kiiroo's FeelConnect-paired devices) that let one partner's movements or input control the other's device in real time — the highest-intimacy device category, and the one most constrained by needing both online at once.
how_it_works: Both partners each need their own compatible Kiiroo device (the platform pairs 'him and her,' 'her and her,' or 'him and him' sets).
Both open the FeelConnect app and connect to each other — per Kiiroo's own site, 'long distance partner play happens live, so both partners need to be connected at the same time.'
Input on one device is relayed in real time to actuate the other.
Because it requires simultaneous presence and full attention from both, it only fits windows where both are free, private, and awake at once.
tools_needed: a matched pair of compatible Kiiroo devices
activities.cost: paid (device price not confirmed this pass; site offers free US shipping over $100)
activities.timezone_friction: The real-time-only requirement rules out every asymmetric window (w1, w3, w4, w5, w8, w9), since each of those has one partner unavailable, sleepy, or public. Only w6 (worth the cost of him staying up) and w7 (the one symmetric day) leave both partners free, private, and awake simultaneously. Israel is not listed among Kiiroo's ~40 shipping destinations (the US is); unlisted destinations are explicitly subject to buyer-side customs per their own shipping policy, so shipping to Israel is unconfirmed and should be treated as a real blocker until confirmed directly with Kiiroo.

activities.name: Yes/No/Maybe So checklist, filled out apart
activities.one_liner: A structured, named sexual-preferences checklist (Scarleteen's 'Yes, No, Maybe So' inventory) each partner fills out alone and compares on a call — turning 'what do you actually want' into a concrete document instead of an improvised conversation.
how_it_works: Each partner gets their own copy (printable PDF or fill-in-online) and completes it independently, in their own time, without discussing it first.
Mark every item across its categories (body boundaries, physical activities, non-physical activities, fantasies, and more) with Y (yes), N (no), M (maybe), IDK, F (fantasy), or N/A.
On a call, go through it together section by section, discussing only where you both want to — skip anything either of you isn't ready to share.
Revisit and re-fill periodically — Scarleteen frames it explicitly as 'a snapshot... and an ever-evolving work in progress,' not a one-time form.
tools_needed: Scarleteen's Yes/No/Maybe So checklist (PDF or online)
activities.timezone_friction: The filling-out half is solo work, which is exactly what an asymmetric free day is for — tagged w8/w9 because each partner completes their half alone on their own day off; the comparison conversation (needing both present) then happens in whatever window works next, so the solo WORK is what actually fills the thin window.

activities.name: Name the mismatch as 'unsolvable,' not broken (Gottman reframe)
activities.one_liner: A clinician-sourced reframing conversation for when the two of you want intimacy at different rates: instead of trying to close the gap, name it as one of Gottman's 'perpetual problems' and run the exercise built for it.
how_it_works: Each partner separately notes: am I generally the higher- or lower-desire partner right now, and is my desire more spontaneous (wanting it out of nowhere) or responsive (wanting it once things are already warm)?

Share those notes — per sex therapist Dr. Jordan Rullo writing for the Gottman Institute, most desire mismatch is a biological/temperament difference, not a relationship failure, so the goal is understanding and coping, not matching.

Run Gottman's 'Dreams Within Conflict' exercise on the gridlock: the higher-desire partner explores the unmet need under wanting more sex (often feeling wanted, feeling connected); the lower-desire partner explores theirs (often feeling accepted, not pressured).
Name explicitly what would make a 'no' feel safe to say without it reading as rejection, before either of you needs to use it.

Treat 'just match your libidos' as the wrong goal to chase — Gottman explicitly frames matching as usually unachievable, and online advice that promises a fix is the most commonly over-recommended, least clinically-supported approach to this problem.
tools_needed: nothing beyond the conversation structure above
activities.timezone_friction: This is the honest core of the category for this couple: their intimacy-appropriate windows (w1, w5, w6) are precisely the ones where one partner is depleted, so a conversation ABOUT that mismatch needs a window where neither is running on empty — only w7 qualifies. Running it in w1 or w6 would replicate the very problem it's meant to solve.

activities.name: Something she leaves as she falls asleep, that he wakes up to
activities.one_liner: She sends something intimate in the last minutes before sleep in NYC; it's the first thing on his phone when he wakes at 5am in Israel — the 7-hour gap used as the delivery mechanism instead of fought against.
how_it_works: In her wind-down window (w1, her side), she writes, records a voice note, or sends a photo meant only for him.
She sends it and goes to sleep — no reply expected, because the point is that it arrives while she's asleep.
He receives it as the first thing when he wakes, alone and unhurried, and can give it real attention rather than a distracted glance.
He can reply in kind before his day starts, so it's waiting for her when she wakes hours later — the exchange completes on its own schedule, never requiring both to be awake at once.
activities.timezone_friction: The same w1 window that makes real-time intimacy hard (she's exhausted, he's just waking) is exactly what makes a message with a built-in delay work — the delay IS the anticipation. Grounded in a 2025 scoping review finding that sexting 'offers an avenue for sustaining sexual connection and intimacy' specifically for separated couples; the overnight-delivery framing itself is this report's own structured design on top of that finding, not something the paper tested directly — see budget_constraint above.

activities.name: One line at her lunch desk
activities.one_liner: A single short, text-only message timed to land during her lunch break — something she can read at a glance at her desk and not answer until much later, so the anticipation carries through the rest of her workday.
how_it_works: He composes one message during his relaxed evening and sends it to land during her lunch (NYC 11am-2pm).
Text only — never a voice note that needs headphones, never a photo that needs privacy to open, nothing beyond a glance at a locked-screen preview.
She doesn't have to respond right away; the point is one line that changes the texture of the rest of her workday, not a conversation.
She can reply properly once she's home, carrying it into whatever window comes next.
activities.timezone_friction: Hard-capped to w4 by design: her lunch break is public/desk-bound with a hard stop, so this is deliberately the smallest possible unit — one line, no reply required, nothing needing privacy or audio to open. Tagged w4 alone because anything longer or richer breaks the discretion constraint.

activities.name: A slow build across his Friday / her Sunday off
activities.one_liner: On the day one partner has entirely free and the other is working, the free partner sends a small escalating series of messages spread across the day, so the working partner opens their phone to a building thread rather than a single ping.
how_it_works: On his Friday off (w8) or her Sunday off (w9), the free partner sends 3-4 short messages spaced across the day rather than one long one.
Each message can build slightly on the last (an image, a line, a voice note) so it reads as a sequence when the working partner finally checks their phone.
The working partner doesn't need to engage in real time — the format is designed to be read all at once, in one connected read-through, whenever their day allows.
The call that evening, once both are free, becomes the payoff for a thread that's been building for hours, rather than the whole activity happening inside the call.
activities.timezone_friction: This directly answers the availability-asymmetry (not energy-asymmetry) that defines w8/w9: one person has the whole day and the other is working, so a single well-timed message under-uses the free day. A sequence spread across hours matches the free partner's actual availability and gives the working partner something cumulative to open on their own schedule.

activities.name: Scheduled sexting as a standing ritual, not a spontaneous event
activities.one_liner: Treat sexting as a recurring, semi-planned ritual rather than something that only happens when the mood spontaneously strikes both of you at once — research on separated couples specifically finds it sustains sexual connection where a purely-spontaneous approach struggles against the schedule.
how_it_works: Pick a recurring slot you can usually protect — after the main call, when both are relaxed and private (w1, w5, or w6/w7).
Treat it like any other ritual on the calendar: a loose, not-mandatory expectation rather than a strict appointment, so it doesn't become a chore.

A 2025 scoping review across 70 studies found sexting is 'associated with greater sexual satisfaction' and facilitates communicating desires/fantasies that are 'often easier to express digitally than verbally' — the format itself, not just the content, is doing work here.
Explicitly agree on device/photo-storage hygiene before it becomes a habit, not after (see privacy findings).
activities.timezone_friction: Tagged to the three windows where at least one partner is private, unhurried, and not about to walk into public — w1 (she's already in bed), w5 (she's home and energized even if he's fading), and w6 (event-grade, worth the cost). Not tagged w4 (too public/short) or w8/w9 (see the dedicated build-up entries for those instead).

activities.name: Explore OMGYES separately, then compare notes
activities.one_liner: A research-backed platform, built with academic partners publishing in the Journal of Sex Research and Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy, for learning specific pleasure techniques — designed for solo exploration, which this couple can repurpose by each going through it separately and comparing findings on a call.
how_it_works: Each partner buys individual access (one-time purchase, not a subscription) and goes through the relevant modules alone and privately.
Note 2-3 specific things that were new or interesting personally — the platform is built around making previously hard-to-articulate preferences 'shareable.'
On a call in an unhurried window, compare notes: what did you each find, what do you want to try, what doesn't apply to you.
This is explicitly NOT a couples/shared-viewing product as designed — you are repurposing an individual education tool as a conversation-starter.
activities.cost: paid (one-time purchase; current price not confirmed this pass)
activities.timezone_friction: The exploration half is solo and can happen whenever either partner has private time; tagged only w7 for the comparison conversation, since that's the one window guaranteed both are free, unhurried, and not depleted.

activities.name: A joint session with an AASECT-certified sex therapist
activities.one_liner: Use AASECT's own referral directory, searchable by country, to find a licensed, board-certified sex therapist and book a joint video session — the professional-help option for when desire mismatch, anxiety, or a specific blocker needs more than a self-guided conversation.
how_it_works: Go to AASECT's Referral Directory and search by country/state and practitioner type (therapist, counselor, or educator).

Look specifically for someone who lists couples work and telehealth/video sessions, since you're not in the same city — confirm this directly with the practitioner, as the directory page itself doesn't state it explicitly.
Book a joint session where both of you are on the same call with the therapist.

Use it for a specific, real blocker (ongoing desire mismatch, resentment about frequency, anxiety about the arrangement) rather than as generic maintenance — this is the escalation path, not the default.
activities.cost: paid (fee varies by therapist; not standardized)
activities.timezone_friction: Needs a scheduled block where both are alert and private at once with a professional third party whose own business hours also have to line up across a 7h gap and a working week — realistically only w7 delivers that reliably.

activities.name: A voice note for the commute, not a call
activities.one_liner: A short, headphones-only voice memo — not a live call — timed for her commute: something with intimate content she can listen to hands-free while walking or on transit, without needing to look at a screen or find privacy.
how_it_works: He records a 2-5 minute voice memo during his relaxed evening, saying what he'd say if they were together, and sends it before her commute window opens.
She plays it through headphones during her walk or commute — audio only, so it survives being interrupted by a crosswalk or a subway entrance.
No response is expected in the moment; if she wants to reply in kind, she can record her own on the way home or later.
This is deliberately NOT a live call — the point is that it works exactly when her hands and eyes are unavailable, which live intimacy never tolerates.
tools_needed: Messages voice memo or Voice Memos app
activities.timezone_friction: Tagged w3 alone: audio-only and screen-free is the entire design constraint of this window, and a voice memo is one of the few intimacy-adjacent formats that survives it — text needs eyes on a screen, a call needs both hands and attention, a photo needs privacy to open. One of the only entries in the whole category built specifically for w3, which is otherwise the correctly-thin cell for this category.

privacy_findings.subject: iMessage content encryption
privacy_findings.finding: Apple states iMessage content and attachments are secured with end-to-end encryption in transit and storage, and that 'Apple can't decrypt the data.'
privacy_findings.practical_implication: Text/photo content sent via iMessage cannot be read by Apple itself in transit — but see the iCloud Backup finding below, which is the actual hole most people miss.

privacy_findings.subject: FaceTime call encryption
privacy_findings.finding: FaceTime audio/video, including Group FaceTime, is end-to-end encrypted (AES-256 in Counter Mode, HMAC-SHA-1 authenticated); Apple states it 'can't decrypt the data.'
privacy_findings.practical_implication: The couple's primary channel is genuinely end-to-end encrypted for the live call itself. This does not cover screen recordings or screenshots taken by either party's own device, which are entirely outside encryption's scope.

privacy_findings.subject: Standard iCloud Backup is NOT end-to-end encrypted — the commonly-missed hole
privacy_findings.finding: With iCloud Backup turned on (the default), Apple states the backup includes a copy of the Messages-in-iCloud encryption key 'so Apple can help the user recover their messages' — meaning Apple itself holds a key that can decrypt backed-up message content. The backup service's own key is 'securely backed up to iCloud Hardware Security Modules in Apple data centers,' i.e. Apple-controlled, not exclusively the user's.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: Anything sent over iMessage is only genuinely end-to-end encrypted for as long as iCloud Backup stays off, or until Advanced Data Protection is turned on. With default settings, a backed-up copy of intimate photos, voice memos, or texts is accessible to Apple, and therefore reachable via a valid legal request to Apple or exposed if Apple's own systems are compromised.

privacy_findings.subject: Advanced Data Protection closes the backup/photos hole, but not completely, and is opt-in
privacy_findings.finding: Turning on Advanced Data Protection raises the number of iCloud data categories under end-to-end encryption from 14 to 23, explicitly including iCloud Backup and Photos. Even with it on, iCloud Calendar, Contacts, Mail, and collaborative Pages/Numbers/Keynote documents remain outside end-to-end encryption.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: If this couple wants their intimate photos and messages to actually be unreadable by Apple, both partners need to individually turn on Advanced Data Protection in Settings — it is opt-in, not default, and it's a per-Apple-ID setting, so one partner enabling it does not protect the other's backup.

privacy_findings.subject: Hidden Photos album is locked by default, but full protection detail unconfirmed
privacy_findings.finding: Apple's own support page, titled 'Hide photos on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple Vision Pro with the Hidden album,' confirms the feature exists; corroborating non-Apple sources describe both the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums as 'locked by default' behind Face ID/Touch ID/passcode. The full body text of Apple's own page could not be retrieved after repeated attempts, so the exact authentication mechanism is confirmed only at medium confidence.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: Hidden is not the same as invisible-to-Apple, and hidden does not mean unlocked-by-default access — treat the Hidden album as a local screen-lock, not an encryption boundary. It does not change any of the iCloud Backup exposure above.

privacy_findings.subject: We-Connect (We-Vibe) has a documented history of undisclosed data collection
privacy_findings.finding: In 2016, independent researchers found the We-Connect app (which controls We-Vibe devices, including for long-distance/remote-control use) collecting usage data without adequate disclosure. Standard Innovation, the manufacturer, settled the resulting class action for approximately $3.2 million in March 2017.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: This is a concrete, sourced precedent, not a hypothetical risk: connected intimacy devices are a documented target for exactly this kind of data exposure. It doesn't mean every device in this category behaves this way today, but it is the reason to actually read a device's privacy policy before connecting an account.

privacy_findings.subject: We-Connect links to a state-specific health-data privacy policy
privacy_findings.finding: We-Vibe's own site links to both a general Privacy Policy and a separate 'Washington Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy' specifically for the We-Connect app.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: The existence of a state-specific consumer-health-data policy signals regulators now treat this category of app data as health data subject to extra protection in at least some US jurisdictions — worth reading the linked policy before connecting an account rather than assuming it's an ordinary app privacy policy.

mediated_intimacy_framing_note: Team-lead relayed a finding from T5 (a 2025 fNIRS hyperscanning study showing video calls measurably reduce interpersonal neural synchrony vs. in-person contact, specifically in romantic couples) — I have not sourced or verified this myself; it is T5's finding, not mine, and I am not asserting it independently here. But it retroactively explains a pattern already visible across this thread: the strongest, most defensible entries are the ones that do NOT try to simulate live presence. t7-overnight-fell-asleep-to-woke-up-to, t7-lunch-break-discreet-anticipation, and t7-friday-sunday-slow-build are all built around asynchronous, delay-based delivery rather than real-time video. t7-totwoo-touch-jewelry and t7-apple-digital-touch-heartbeat are silent, momentary, non-video touch signals. None of these are trying to be a worse version of being in the same room — they use a channel property video doesn't have (arriving exactly when the other person is alone and receptive, or landing as a felt sensation with zero visual/cognitive load). The one entry in this set that DOES require live simultaneous presence and full attention — t7-app-controlled-toy-realtime-overlap (Kiiroo) — is also the one most tightly window-constrained (only w6/w7), which is consistent with this framing: the harder something leans on simulating co-presence, the fewer windows in this couple's actual week it survives. Suggest this as the organizing idea for how the site introduces the intimacy shelf: not 'the next best thing to being there,' but 'things this medium can do that presence can't' — that framing is CPO/Design-Lead's call, not mine, but it falls directly out of this thread's own data.
gaps: Lovense's shipping-to-Israel status could not be confirmed: attempted lovense.com/long-distance-sex-toys, /faq, /shipping-info (404), /shipping-policy (404), and /faq/Shipping/ (loaded but returned only navigation, no policy text), plus a DuckDuckGo search that surfaced only third-party reshipping-forwarder pages (MyUS, ParcelMonkey) rather than an official answer. UNKNOWN — treat as unconfirmed, not as 'yes.'
Lovense's sync mechanics (real-time-only vs. asynchronous/scheduled control, cellular vs. wifi-only) could not be confirmed from official documentation within budget. UNKNOWN.

Kiiroo's Israel shipping status: Israel does not appear on their ~40-country shipping list, but this was not confirmed as an explicit exclusion (vs. simply unlisted/uncommon) — I did not contact Kiiroo directly. Treated as a probable but not certain blocker.

Community-sourced content (reddit.com/r/LongDistance) was largely inaccessible: www.reddit.com, old.reddit.com, and the Reddit JSON API endpoint all returned fetch errors in this environment for every URL attempted. I could see thread TITLES via DuckDuckGo search snippets (e.g. 'Tips on how to keep your LDR ~spicy~,' 'What is intimacy like in LDR?', 'Lack of physical intimacy in LDR') but never verified actual comment content, so none of those threads were used as a source for any claim in this report, per the no-fabrication rule. This is a real gap relative to the brief's instruction to prioritize community consensus with permalinks.

App Store privacy-label verification for Kiiroo, Lovense, and We-Vibe's apps (an explicit privacy must_cover item — app-permission/cloud-relay model) could not be completed: I could not reliably discover the correct official app listings without search. Two candidates were checked directly and rejected as unconfirmed/wrong (see budget_constraint above). A round-2 pass needs either working search or hand-supplied correct App Store URLs for: the We-Connect app (Standard Innovation/WOW Tech), Lovense Remote (developer: HYTTO PTE. LTD. per a third-party app-tracking site, unverified directly), and Kiiroo's FeelConnect app.

Apple's own documentation on Digital Touch's distance/connectivity mechanism (Bluetooth-proximity vs. internet/iMessage delivery) could not be retrieved directly after three attempts at different Apple support URLs, which returned truncated or unrelated content. The entry in this report is sourced to converging tech-press descriptions instead and capped at medium confidence for that reason.

iMessage screenshot-notification behavior (whether the sender is told if the recipient screenshots a photo) could not be sourced to a page I was able to actually open: two candidate pages (MacReports, AirDroid) 404'd, and the specific Apple support URL tried (HT207981) also 404'd. Deliberately NOT included as a privacy_finding because I could not verify it against a source I actually opened. Worth checking directly in Settings before relying on it.
OMGYES's current pricing and whether the platform has added an explicit couples/shared-viewing mode since its original solo-education design were not verified beyond the research page fetched.

AASECT's referral directory was confirmed searchable by country, but I could not confirm from the directory page itself whether listed practitioners explicitly offer cross-border telehealth (a US-licensed therapist seeing a couple where one partner is physically in Israel carries its own licensing complexity a couple would need to raise directly with any therapist they contact).

WebSearch (the tool this brief specifies as the standard discovery mechanism) was unavailable for essentially this entire thread — see budget_constraint block above for full detail and what it specifically cost.
confidence_summary: MEDIUM. The technical core — Apple's E2E encryption architecture for iMessage/FaceTime, the iCloud Backup/Advanced Data Protection distinction, and the primary research citations (Van Dijck et al. 2025 on sexting; Hofer et al. 2020 on partner scent and sleep) — is HIGH confidence, verified directly from Apple's own security documentation and named peer-reviewed sources. Device-shipping claims are mixed: Totwoo's Israel shipping is confirmed HIGH from their own policy page; Bond Touch's non-coverage of Israel is confirmed HIGH; Kiiroo and Lovense are UNKNOWN/unconfirmed despite repeated attempts. Several secondary privacy details (Hidden album mechanics, screenshot notification, App Store privacy labels) were constrained by fetch failures/discovery failures and are capped at MEDIUM or moved to gaps rather than asserted. The single biggest limiting factor across the whole thread was WebSearch being unavailable for essentially the entire session — see budget_constraint.
